journal:
# Noura (p07) journal

## Day 1 (Sun)
Weekend. Installed the app but did not open it. Family day, ate a lot, nothing logged.

## Day 2 (Mon)
- Opened the app first time. Welcome screen short and clear. Profile form: 160 cm, 41, 83.8 kg, female, lightly active, "yes" eating same for 2+ weeks. The weight I typed in the profile was saved as today's weigh-in automatically — good, no double entry.
- iPhone "Add to Home Screen" banner — I tapped Got it.
- Logged 4 meals in Nutrition → + Food, one popup per meal. Easy.
- Confused: the protein bar had no macros and after I added it the "Day total" line dropped the protein/carbs/fat totals and showed only kcal. I thought my macros got erased.
- Ticked "Day complete" at night.
- App started on "Maintain" (target = 2,020 = maintenance). I had to find the ⚙ on Nutrition to switch to Lose. Default 0.5%/week → target 1,560 kcal. Nobody asked me my goal in the setup — I'd expect that in the profile.
- Protein target 115 g "× 64 kg reference weight" — I weigh 84, what is 64? Didn't bother to read more.
## Day 3 (Tue)
- Tapped "Weight" on the home screen expecting to add my weight — it opened the weight chart instead. The add button is the small "+ Weight" one. Found it after closing the chart.
- Weight form pre-fills date and time, nice. 83.7 saved, shows ▼0.1 kg.
- Meals logged, day ticked complete. When one meal only has protein, the day total shows kcal + protein only (carbs/fat vanish). Slightly odd but fine.
## Day 4 (Wed)
- Scale 83.2. Home shows "▼ 0.6 kg" (vs first) but "Trend weight 83.7". Two different numbers, I just look at the arrow.
- Recommendation box still says "on-track check needs 14 days of data (day 1 so far)" — it's my 3rd day. Says updated weekly on Monday so I guess it's frozen. Confusing "day 1".
- "Protein averaged 80 g on 2 logged day(s) vs 115 g target" — I logged 3 days. I think Monday didn't count because the protein bar had no macros. Not explained. 115 g protein sounds like a lot for me.
## Day 5 (Thu)
- Shawarma had no macros, logged just kcal. Fine.
- Nutrition page now says protein "average of 2 complete day(s) with protein logged" — ok, so days with a meal without macros don't count for protein. Makes sense once written there.
- Avg intake 1,517 vs target 1,560 — I'm under on weekdays. Good.
## Day 6 (Fri)
- Normal day, 4 meals, complete. Scale up to 83.2 again from 82.9 — app still says trend 83.6, so I don't panic.
## Day 7 (Sat)
- Weekend, didn't open the app. Ate ~2,400 with family. I'll do my weekly look on Monday since that's when the app updates and I don't touch my phone for this on weekends.
## Week 1 (checked Mon day 9, 2026-10-12, before logging)
- App said: maintenance 2,050 ± 480 kcal, "Estimated", 0% from my data. Target 1,580 (lose 0.5%/wk). Avg intake 1,574 (4 of last 7 days complete). Weight trend -0.45 kg/week (95%: -0.90 to ~0). Protein 83 g vs 115 g. No warnings.
- After I logged Monday's meals the same screen changed to maintenance 2,010 ± 470, target 1,550, "5% from your data". It says "updated weekly on Monday" — so I thought it was fixed for the week, but it moved again the same day. A bit confusing, but it's still Monday so maybe ok.
- What I understood: I eat ~1,570 on weekdays, target is ~1,550–1,580, so I'm on target and losing almost half a kilo a week. Great.
- Note: the app shows my weekends as "not logged" and says nothing about them. It doesn't tell me that my big weekend meals matter. I'm not changing anything. No plan change.
- Did not read "Explain the math" — no time.
## Days 8–15 (script for my weekday routine; weekends untouched)
- 10-15 the Nutrition page showed: "macros add up to ~1076 kcal vs 1471 kcal logged (27% apart). One of the numbers may be off." I typed exactly what the packets/app said. I don't know which one is wrong and I don't have time to check. Ignored it. It stayed on the screen for days after.
- Monday–Friday weigh-ins keep bouncing 82.5–83.9. The trend line is calmer (83.6 → 83.4).

## Week 2 (checked Mon day 16, 2026-10-19)
- App said: "On track. Your estimated rate (−0.83 to −0.03 kg/week) includes your target of −0.42 kg/week. Suggested intake 1,590 kcal/day." Maintenance 2,050 ± 440, Estimated, 13% from my data. Avg intake 1,561 (4 of last 7 days complete). Protein 72 g vs 115 g (only 3 days counted — one dinner had no macros).
- What I understood: "On track" = keep doing what I do. That's all I needed. Short and clear.
- Decision: no change. (The app still says nothing about my weekends being blank.)
- Week 2 note: on Monday 10-19 morning it said suggested 1,590; after I logged that Monday's weigh-in and meals, it said 1,490 and maintenance 1,950 (22% from data). "Updated weekly on Monday" but it changed twice on the same Monday. Which number is my number for the week?

## Week 3 (checked Mon day 23, 2026-10-26, before logging)
- App said: "On track. Estimated rate −0.69 to +0 kg/week includes your target −0.42. Suggested intake 1,570." Maintenance 2,030 ± 390, Estimated, 34% from my data. Avg intake 1,757 (4 of 7 days complete). Trend −0.34 kg/wk. Protein 103 g vs 115 g.
- What I understood: it says On track, so fine. I did notice my average (1,757) is almost 200 above the suggested 1,570, yet it still says On track. Mixed message, but I go with the big words "On track".
- Decision: no change.
- Scale today 81.5 — lowest ever, happy.
- Week 3 note: again same-Monday jump — morning 1,570 suggested / 2,030 maintenance, after logging Monday: 1,680 / 2,140. Moves by 100+ kcal within one day even though it says weekly.

## Week 4 (checked Mon day 30, 2026-11-02, before logging)
- App said: "On track. −0.70 to −0.11 kg/week includes target −0.41. Suggested intake 1,610." Maintenance 2,070 ± 330, now labelled "Measured" (53% from my data). Avg intake 1,517. Trend −0.40 kg/wk. Protein 74 g vs 115 g.
- What I understood: the word changed from Estimated to Measured, so now it "knows" me. On track again. 
- Scale this morning 83.5 — after the weekend it's always up (Monday 83.6, 83.7, 83.5…), then Friday it's 82.5. The app never mentions this pattern. I wonder if the app knows I eat more on weekends — it only shows "not logged" for Sat/Sun and never asked me. If its "Measured" maintenance is based only on my weekdays, is it right? No idea.
- Decision: no change — "On track".
- Week 4 note: same Monday jump again: morning 1,610 / 2,070 → after my Monday weigh-in (always high after the weekend) 1,480 / 1,940.

## Week 5 (checked Mon day 37, 2026-11-09, before logging)
- A yellow note at top: "It's been 30+ days since your last backup" → I tapped Back up now → "Full backup (JSON)" → file downloaded (downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-11-09.json). Counts shown: 25 weigh-ins, 100 food entries, 25 complete days. Good, reassuring.
- App said: "On track… Suggested intake 1,460". Then a long paragraph: "The math gives 1457 kcal/day, which is below the minimum this app will suggest (1463…). The target is set to 1463; expect slower progress than the chosen rate." Maintenance 1,910 ± 280, Measured. Label says "lose · 0.5%/wk · at minimum".
- Confused: it says "On track" AND "expect slower progress" in the same box. Also the paragraph says 1463 but the big number says 1,460. My target has gone 1,560 → 1,460 in five weeks while I'm eating the same — why does my maintenance keep going down? 1,910 for a woman my size sounds low.
- I opened "Explain the math" once: way too long (Hall 2008, Forbes, MAD…). One line I did get: days I don't log are assumed to be like the average of my logged days. But my weekends are NOT like my weekdays — I eat much more. So I think the app believes I eat less than I do, and that's why it says my maintenance is low. Nothing in the app ever asked or warned me about this.
- Decision: headline says On track. I'm not changing my eating. Screenshot: screens/1790458055090.png, math: screens/1790458075073.png
- Same Monday evening, after logging: the box flipped from "On track" to "Your estimated rate (−0.41 to +0.05) doesn't include your target of −0.42. Eating about 260 kcal/day less than recently would close the gap. Suggested intake 1,460." Maintenance now 1,830 ± 260. Morning said On track, evening says not on track — same "weekly" update. Screenshot screens/1790458106624.png.
- Decision: OK, clear instruction — eat ~260 less. plan 1460 "app said eat 260 less, suggested 1,460" (my weekdays). Weekends are family time, those stay as they are.
## Days 38–43
- Ate ~1,370–1,445 on weekdays as the app asked. Weekends as usual (not opened). Tuesday after the weekend the scale said 84.1 — the highest since I started. Very discouraging, the app said nothing about it.

## Week 6 (checked Mon day 44, 2026-11-16)
- App said: "On track. −0.48 to +0.07 kg/week includes target −0.42. Suggested intake 1,470." Plus the "math gives 1360, below the minimum… target set to 1465; expect slower progress" paragraph. Maintenance 1,820 ± 300, Measured 61%. Avg intake 1,413. Trend only −0.21 kg/week. After logging Monday: 1,800 maintenance, trend −0.19.
- What I understood: I'm already at the lowest the app will allow. My maintenance keeps dropping (2,050 → 1,800). I eat 1,400 on weekdays and I'm losing only 0.2 kg a week. The app says "On track" but the range goes up to +0.07 — so I might not be losing at all? Confusing that that's "On track".
- The app never once said "you have no food logged on weekends" or "your weight jumps every Monday". I have a feeling my weekends are the problem, but the app doesn't help me see it.
- Decision: can't go lower than the minimum, keep plan ~1,460 on weekdays. No plan change.
## Week 7 (checked Mon day 51, 2026-11-23)
- App said: On track, −0.54 to −0.05 kg/week, suggested 1,460 (still "at minimum", same long paragraph). Maintenance 1,830 ± 270, Measured 68%. Avg intake 1,479. Trend −0.30 kg/week. Protein 83 g vs 115 g (it keeps telling me protein is low, but never tells me what to eat — I just ignore it).
- Understood: same as last week. The long "math gives 1371…" paragraph is the same every week, I stopped reading it.
- Decision: no change. Keep weekdays ~1,460.
## Week 8 (checked Mon day 58, 2026-11-30)
- App said: On track (−0.53 to −0.08 kg/wk), suggested 1,460 (at minimum, "math gives 1325"). Maintenance 1,780 ± 250, Measured 73%. Avg intake 1,396. Trend −0.31 kg/wk.
- Understood: maintenance still sliding down (now 1,780). Eating 1,400 on weekdays for weeks and my trend weight only went ~83.8 → ~82.6 in 2 months. The app keeps saying On track, so I keep going.
- Decision: no change.
## Week 9 (checked Mon day 65, 2026-12-07)
- App said: On track (−0.50 to −0.08), suggested 1,460 at minimum ("math gives 1344"). Maintenance 1,800 ± 230, Measured 76%. Avg intake 1,579 (a couple of bigger weekday dinners). Trend −0.29 kg/wk.
- Scale 81.6 today — nice Monday for once.
- Decision: no change.
## Week 10 (checked Mon day 72, 2026-12-14)
- Backup reminder came back on Wed 12-09 (30 days after my first backup) and stayed every day until I dealt with it. I tapped Back up now → Full backup again on Monday.
- App said: On track (−0.45 to −0.05), suggested 1,450 at minimum ("math gives 1347"). Maintenance 1,800 ± 220, Measured. Trend weight around 82.
- Scale has been in the 81s on some days. Slow, but moving.
- Decision: no change.
## Week 11 (checked Mon day 79, 2026-12-21)
- App said: On track (−0.42 to −0.06), suggested 1,450 at minimum ("math gives 1290"). Maintenance 1,740 ± 190, Measured 83%. Avg intake 1,491. Trend −0.24 kg/week.
- Understood: my "maintenance" is now 1,740 — started at 2,050. The range got narrower (±190) so the app is more and more sure of a number that I suspect is wrong, because it never sees my weekends. If I ate 1,740 every day I bet I'd gain.
- Decision: no change, I'm already at the app's minimum.
## Days 73–84
- Normal weekdays, weekends not opened. Scale reached 81.2 on the last Friday. Trend 81.5 kg (started 83.8). ~2.3 kg in 12 weeks.

## End (Sat day 84, evening — I opened it one last time for the backup)
- ⇩ on the home screen → "Your data": 60 weigh-ins, 240 food entries, 60 complete days. Full backup (JSON) → downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-12-26.json. "Export daily data (JSON)" → downloads/bodytracker-daily_2026-10-05_to_2026-12-25.json.
- Opened the daily file: one block per day with weight and calories. Only my weekdays are in it — weekends simply don't exist. Some days show protein but no carbs/fat (when one meal had only protein), some days no macros at all. The file is readable but it's for a computer, not for me.
- Body composition card said "Not enough data yet" all 12 weeks (I never had a body-fat scale or tape) — it's the first big box on the home screen and was useless for me.

## Possible bugs / problems
1. "Updated weekly on Monday" but the numbers change on Monday itself after I log that Monday's weigh-in/food. 10-19: 1,590 → 1,490. 10-26: 1,570 → 1,680. 11-02: 1,610 → 1,480. 11-09: morning "On track" (screens/1790458055090.png) → evening "doesn't include your target… eat about 260 kcal/day less" (screens/1790458106624.png). Expected one number for the week.
2. I never log Saturday/Sunday (12 weeks in a row) and my Monday weigh-in is always the highest of the week. The app never pointed this out. "Explain the math" says blank days are assumed to be like my logged days. Maintenance went 2,050 → 1,740 while the ± range got smaller and the label said "Measured 83%". I think it is sure about a number that's too low, because it doesn't know about my weekend eating. It pushed my target down to the minimum (1,450–1,460).
3. The same box says "On track" and "expect slower progress than the chosen rate" (from 11-09 on). Weeks 6 and 9 said "On track" even though the range went up to +0.07 kg/week, i.e. maybe not losing at all.
4. Headline says 1,460 but the paragraph under it says 1463 / 1464 / 1457 (small rounding mismatch).
5. First week: "An on-track check needs 14 days of data (day 1 so far)" stayed "day 1" from Monday through Friday.
6. The "macros add up to ~1076 vs 1471 kcal" note for 10-15 stayed on the Nutrition page for about a week.
7. Text spacing: "36 day s", "25 daily weight s", "60 day s with data" (Explain the math, Your data).

## Final review
The logging part is quick — I could do a meal in a few taps and ticking "Day complete" at night became a habit. The weekly "On track" line was the only thing I really read and I liked that it's short. But after three months I lost only about 2 kg eating ~1,450 on weekdays, and the app kept telling me I'm "On track" while quietly lowering my maintenance until I hit its minimum. It never told me the obvious thing: "you never log weekends and your weight jumps every Monday — your weekends are probably cancelling your weekdays." The long math paragraphs are not for a mom with three kids. Goal (lose/maintain) should be asked in setup, not hidden in the ⚙. Would I keep using it? Maybe — for logging, yes; for advice, I don't fully trust it.
agentReply:
# p07 (Noura, 41 F, 160 cm, 84 kg): final report

## 1. Usage
- 84 simulated days (2026-10-04 to 2026-12-26). I used the app on 60 weekdays (Mon–Fri, weeks 1–12) and opened it once on day 84 (a Saturday) for the backup and export. I never opened it on any other weekend day.
- Meals logged: 240 (4 per weekday). Days marked complete: 60. Weigh-ins: 60 (the first one came from the profile weight).
- I changed my eating once: `plan 1460` on 11-09, when the app said "eat ~260 kcal/day less".
- Trend weight went from 83.8 to 81.5 kg (about −0.2 kg/week against a target of −0.42 kg/week).

## 2. Weekly table (checked each Monday morning, then again after logging that Monday)
| week | maintenance shown | target | label | recommendation (short) | what I did |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (10-12) | 2,050 ±480 → 2,010 ±470 | 1,580 → 1,550 | Estimated 0→5% | Suggested intake; on-track check needs 14 days | nothing |
| 2 (10-19) | 2,050 ±440 → 1,950 ±420 | 1,590 → 1,490 | Estimated 13→22% | On track | nothing |
| 3 (10-26) | 2,030 ±390 → 2,140 ±360 | 1,570 → 1,680 | Estimated 34% | On track (while avg intake 1,757 > target) | nothing |
| 4 (11-02) | 2,070 ±330 → 1,940 ±300 | 1,610 → 1,480 | Measured 53→60% | On track | nothing |
| 5 (11-09) | 1,910 ±280 → 1,830 ±260 | 1,460 (at minimum) | Measured 71% | morning: On track + "below minimum, expect slower progress"; evening: not on track, eat ~260 less | backed up (reminder); plan 1460 |
| 6 (11-16) | 1,820 ±300 → 1,800 ±280 | 1,470 → 1,460 (min) | Measured 61–65% | On track, at minimum | nothing |
| 7 (11-23) | 1,830 ±270 | 1,460 (min) | Measured 68% | On track, at minimum | nothing |
| 8 (11-30) | 1,780 ±250 | 1,460 (min) | Measured 73% | On track, at minimum | nothing |
| 9 (12-07) | 1,800 ±230 | 1,460 → 1,450 (min) | Measured 76% | On track, at minimum | nothing |
| 10 (12-14) | 1,800 ±220 | 1,450 (min) | Measured | On track, at minimum; backup reminder | backed up |
| 11 (12-21) | 1,740 ±190 | 1,450 (min) | Measured 83% | On track, at minimum | nothing |

## 3. Confusions
- Setup: it never asked for my goal. The app started on "Maintain" (target = maintenance), and I had to find the ⚙ on Nutrition to switch to Lose.
- Home screen: tapping "Weight" opened the chart. The add button is the small "+ Weight".
- Food log: when one meal had no macros, the day total dropped the carbs and fat (or all macros). I thought they had been erased.
- Protein "× 64 kg reference weight": I weigh 84 kg, so I didn't know what 64 meant.
- Protein line "on 2 logged day(s)" when I had logged 3 days. Days with a meal missing macros are left out, and this is only explained further down.
- Week 1 recommendation said "(day 1 so far)" every day from Monday to Friday.
- "Updated weekly on Monday", but the numbers changed again after I logged on Monday itself.
- The same box said "On track" and "expect slower progress than the chosen rate".
- "On track" was shown while the rate range reached +0.07 kg/week.
- In week 3 my average intake (1,757) was about 190 above the target (1,570), and the box still said "On track".
- The "Explain the math" screen is far too long (Hall 2008, Forbes, MAD) for a busy person.
- The "Body composition: Not enough data yet" card is the biggest box on the home screen and showed nothing useful for 12 weeks.
- A macro-mismatch note ("1076 vs 1471 kcal") stayed on the page for about a week, and I couldn't tell what to do about it.

## 4. Possible bugs
1. **The weekly update isn't stable on the update day.**
   - Steps: open Nutrition on Monday before weighing and read the number. Then log that Monday's weigh-in and meals and read it again.
   - Expected: one number that holds for the whole week.
   - Actual: the target moved 1,590→1,490 (10-19), 1,570→1,680 (10-26) and 1,610→1,480 (11-02). On 11-09 the box flipped from "On track" to "doesn't include your target… eat about 260 kcal/day less".
   - Screenshots: screens/1790458055090.png (morning) and screens/1790458106624.png (evening).
2. **Weekends that are never logged skew maintenance down, and the app gives no warning.**
   - Steps: for 12 weeks, log every weekday and never log Sat/Sun (eating more on those days). Monday weigh-ins are always the highest of the week.
   - Expected: a note saying the weekends are missing and the estimate assumes they match my weekdays.
   - Actual: nothing was said. Maintenance fell from 2,050 to 1,740 while the ± range narrowed and the label read "Measured 83%". The target was pinned at the minimum (1,450–1,460), and weekly loss was about half the target while the app kept saying "On track".
   - Screenshot: screens/1790458881731.png.
3. **The headline target and the paragraph under it disagree slightly.** The headline says 1,460, while the paragraph says 1463, 1464 or 1457 in different weeks. See screens/1790458055090.png.
4. **"(day 1 so far)" didn't count up during week 1** (days 3–6). See screens/1790457394587.png.
5. **Spacing typos:** "36 day s", "25 daily weight s" and "60 day s with data". See screens/1790458075073.png and screens/1790459027722.png.
6. **The two exports use different time formats.** The daily export's `exportedAt` is in local time (+03:00) and the backup's is in UTC (Z). This is minor.

## 5. Review
Logging is quick, and the short "On track" line was all I needed on a busy day. But in three months I lost only about 2 kg on around 1,450 kcal on weekdays. The app kept saying "On track" while it quietly lowered my maintenance until it hit its own minimum. It never told me that I don't log weekends and my weight jumps every Monday, which I think is my real problem. **Would keep using: maybe.** I'd keep it for logging, but I don't trust the advice.
